q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(DISTINCT P.EMPLOYEE_ID), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(DISTINCT P.EMPLOYEE_ID), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPLOYEE_ID, NAME, EXPERIENCE_YEARS) VALUES (1, 'Employee1', 10), (2, 'Employee2', 20); INSERT INTO PROJECT (PROJECT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2);
explanation: Q1 calculates the average experience years of employees for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of employees in the project. Q2, on the other hand, calculates the average experience years by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of distinct employees in the project, which can be different from the number of employees if an employee is assigned to multiple projects.
counterexample_dsp: A project with two employees, where one employee has 10 years of experience and the other has 20 years of experience. The average experience years calculated by Q1 and Q2 should be different due to the difference in the number of employees and distinct employees in the project.
